Flu.description: Influenza (flu) is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses that infect the nose, throat, and sometimes the lungs.
Flu.detailed_advice: Most people with the flu have mild illness. Stay home and rest. Drink plenty of fluids and manage fever with medications.
self_care: Take acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever and aches
Flu.when_to_see_doctor: Seek medical attention if you experience difficulty breathing, chest pain, sudden dizziness, or severe vomiting.

Common Cold.description: The common cold is a viral infection of your nose and throat. It's usually harmless and resolves within 7-10 days.
Common Cold.detailed_advice: There's no cure for the common cold. Treatment is directed at relieving signs and symptoms.
self_care: Soothe a sore throat with saltwater gargle
Common Cold.when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor if symptoms last more than 10 days or if you have a high fever above 103°F.

Fever.description: Fever is an elevated body temperature, usually due to an infection. A normal body temperature is around 98.6°F.
Fever.detailed_advice: Fever is usually a sign your body is fighting infection. Rest and hydration are important.
Fever.when_to_see_doctor: Seek attention if fever exceeds 103°F, lasts over 3 days, or is accompanied by confusion or difficulty breathing.

Headache.description: A headache is pain in the head or neck, often caused by stress, tension, or infections.
Headache.detailed_advice: Most headaches are manageable with rest and pain relievers. Identify and avoid triggers.
Headache.when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor for sudden severe headache, headache with fever/stiff neck, or increasing frequency.

Cough.description: A cough clears airways of mucus, dust, or irritants. Causes include infections, allergies, or environmental factors.
Cough.detailed_advice: Most coughs resolve on their own. Stay hydrated and rest. Over-the-counter syrups may help.
Cough.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if cough lasts over 3 weeks, you cough up blood, or have shortness of breath.

Cough and Cold.description: Combination of cold and cough symptoms from viral infection affecting the respiratory tract.
Cough and Cold.detailed_advice: Rest and fluids are primary treatment. Symptoms typically resolve within 1-2 weeks.
Cough and Cold.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if symptoms persist over 2 weeks or if you develop difficulty breathing.

Sore Throat.description: Scratchy or painful sensation in the throat, often from viral or bacterial infections.
Sore Throat.detailed_advice: Most sore throats are viral and resolve on their own. Gargle with salt water and use throat lozenges.
Sore Throat.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if sore throat lasts over a week, if difficulty swallowing, or if accompanied by high fever.

Migraine.description: Severe throbbing headache, usually on one side, often with nausea and light/sound sensitivity.
Migraine.detailed_advice: Rest in quiet, dark room. Apply compresses. Avoid triggers like stress or certain foods.
Migraine.when_to_see_doctor: Seek immediate attention for severe thunderclap headache or headache with fever/confusion/vision changes.

Allergies.description: Immune reaction to harmless substances, causing sneezing, itching, rashes, or swelling.
Allergies.detailed_advice: Identify and avoid allergens. Over-the-counter antihistamines provide relief.
Allergies.when_to_see_doctor: Seek immediate care for difficulty breathing, swelling of lips/throat, or severe allergic reactions.

Asthma.description: Chronic airway disease with inflammation, causing airflow obstruction and breathing difficulties.
Asthma.detailed_advice: Use prescribed inhalers as directed. Identify and avoid triggers like allergens or cold air.
Asthma.when_to_see_doctor: Seek emergency care for severe difficulty breathing, chest pain, or cyanosis (blue lips/fingers).

Gastroenteritis.description: Inflammation of stomach and intestines from viral or bacterial infection, causing nausea and diarrhea.
Gastroenteritis.detailed_advice: Stay hydrated and rest. Gradually introduce bland foods. Avoid dairy and fatty foods initially.
Gastroenteritis.when_to_see_doctor: Seek attention for severe dehydration, bloody stools, high fever, or symptoms over 3 days.

Diarrhea.description: Loose or watery stools from infections, food intolerances, or medications.
Diarrhea.detailed_advice: Stay hydrated using water, electrolyte solutions, or clear fluids. Gradually reintroduce solid foods.
Diarrhea.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if diarrhea lasts over 3 days, if severe dehydration, or if stools contain blood.

Constipation.description: Infrequent bowel movements or difficulty passing stools from low fiber or dehydration.
Constipation.detailed_advice: Increase fiber gradually, drink more water, and stay active. Establish a regular bowel routine.
Constipation.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if constipation lasts over 3 weeks or if accompanied by severe pain or blood.

Nausea and Vomiting.description: Uncomfortable stomach feeling and forceful expulsion of contents from infections or motion sickness.
Nausea and Vomiting.detailed_advice: Eat small frequent meals and stay hydrated. Ginger and peppermint may help.
Nausea and Vomiting.when_to_see_doctor: Seek attention if vomiting lasts over a few hours or inability to keep fluids down.

Heartburn.description: Burning chest sensation from stomach acid backing into the esophagus.
Heartburn.detailed_advice: Avoid trigger foods like spicy, fatty items. Eat smaller meals and don't eat close to bedtime.
Heartburn.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if heartburn is frequent (over twice weekly) or symptoms don't improve with medication.

Abdominal Pain.description: Pain in the stomach area from conditions ranging from minor gas to serious appendicitis.
Abdominal Pain.detailed_advice: Identify pain location and quality. Rest and apply heat if helpful. Avoid solid foods until pain subsides.
Abdominal Pain.when_to_see_doctor: Seek immediate attention for severe pain, pain with fever, or pain that worsens.

Back Pain.description: Pain in the back muscles, nerves, or discs from poor posture, strain, or herniated discs.
Back Pain.detailed_advice: Rest and apply heat or cold to affected area. Gradually resume normal activities with proper positioning.
Back Pain.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if pain lasts over 6 weeks, if accompanied by numbness, or loss of bladder/bowel control.

Muscle Pain.description: Pain from exercise, tension, injury, or illness affecting muscles in legs, arms, back, or throughout body.
Muscle Pain.detailed_advice: Rest the affected muscle, apply ice or heat, and gradually return to normal activity.
self_care: Apply ice first 48 hours then heat
Muscle Pain.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if pain is severe, doesn't improve in days, or is accompanied by fever.

Joint Pain.description: Discomfort in joints like knees, hips, ankles, elbows from arthritis, injury, inflammation, or joint disorders. Common in legs, neck, back.
Joint Pain.detailed_advice: Rest joint, apply ice or heat, and use anti-inflammatory medications. Physical therapy helps.
Joint Pain.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if pain is severe, swelling doesn't reduce, or movement is significantly limited.

Arthritis.description: Inflammation of one or more joints like knees, hips, ankles causing pain and stiffness in legs, hands, back. Includes osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis.
Arthritis.detailed_advice: Maintain healthy weight, exercise within limits, and use heat/cold therapy. Follow treatment plans.
Arthritis.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor for persistent joint pain, swelling, or stiffness lasting over weeks.

Hypertension.description: High blood pressure increasing risk of heart disease and stroke.
Hypertension.detailed_advice: Monitor pressure regularly, reduce sodium, and take medications as prescribed. Lifestyle changes crucial.
Hypertension.when_to_see_doctor: Seek urgent care if blood pressure exceeds 180/120 with chest pain or vision changes.

Anemia.description: Insufficient red blood cells or hemoglobin reducing oxygen transport throughout the body.
Anemia.detailed_advice: Treatment depends on cause. Iron supplementation, vitamin B12, or folate recommended.
Anemia.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor for persistent fatigue, shortness of breath, or dizziness.

Insomnia.description: Persistent difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or poor sleep quality.
Insomnia.detailed_advice: Establish sleep hygiene: consistent schedule, cool dark room, no screens before bed. Therapy is effective.
Insomnia.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if insomnia persists over a month or significantly affects daytime function.

Anxiety.description: Persistent worry, nervousness, and physical tension ranging from mild to severe.
Anxiety.detailed_advice: Practice relaxation techniques, deep breathing, and mindfulness. Professional therapy very helpful.
Anxiety.when_to_see_doctor: Seek help if anxiety interferes with work, school, or daily activities.

Depression.description: Mental health condition with persistent low mood, loss of interest, and feelings of worthlessness.
Depression.detailed_advice: Treatment involves therapy and/or medication. Professional help important.
Depression.when_to_see_doctor: Seek immediate help if you have thoughts of self-harm or suicide.

Stress.description: Physical and psychological response to life challenges; chronic stress can harm health.
Stress.detailed_advice: Identify stressors and develop coping strategies. Relaxation and lifestyle changes help.
Stress.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if stress causes physical symptoms or affects quality of life.

Acne.description: Common skin condition with pimples, blackheads, whiteheads on face, chest, or back.
Acne.detailed_advice: Maintain good skin hygiene. Over-the-counter products with benzoyl peroxide or salicylic acid often help.
Acne.when_to_see_doctor: See dermatologist if acne is severe or over-the-counter treatments don't help after 6-8 weeks.

Eczema.description: Chronic inflammatory skin condition causing itching, redness, and dry skin.
Eczema.detailed_advice: Keep skin moisturized, avoid harsh soaps and triggers. Use prescribed creams.
Eczema.when_to_see_doctor: See dermatologist if eczema is severe, doesn't improve, or becomes infected.

Psoriasis.description: Chronic autoimmune skin condition causing thick, scaly skin patches.
Psoriasis.detailed_advice: Moisturize regularly and avoid stress triggers. Topical treatments and phototherapy effective.
Psoriasis.when_to_see_doctor: See dermatologist for treatment planning and monitoring.

Urinary Tract Infection.description: Infection of the urinary system including urethra, bladder, ureters, or kidneys.
Urinary Tract Infection.detailed_advice: Drink plenty of water and cranberry juice. Antibiotics usually needed for treatment.
Urinary Tract Infection.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor with UTI symptoms, especially if accompanied by fever or back pain.

Kidney Stones.description: Hard mineral deposits in kidneys causing severe pain.
Kidney Stones.detailed_advice: Stay hydrated and manage pain. Small stones may pass on their own.
Kidney Stones.when_to_see_doctor: Seek care for kidney stone pain, especially with fever, nausea, or inability to urinate.

High Cholesterol.description: Elevated cholesterol increasing risk of heart disease and stroke.
High Cholesterol.detailed_advice: Reduce dietary cholesterol. Regular exercise and weight management important.
High Cholesterol.when_to_see_doctor: Have cholesterol checked regularly, especially with risk factors.

Thyroid Issues.description: Disorders including hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism affecting metabolism and energy.
Thyroid Issues.detailed_advice: Regular monitoring of thyroid function essential. Medications adjust hormone levels.
Thyroid Issues.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor for thyroid symptoms like fatigue, weight changes, or temperature sensitivity.

Pneumonia.description: Lung infection causing inflammation and fluid accumulation in air sacs.
Pneumonia.detailed_advice: Medical treatment often necessary. Rest, hydration, and antibiotics for bacterial pneumonia important.
Pneumonia.when_to_see_doctor: Seek immediate care for severe pneumonia or underlying health conditions.

Bronchitis.description: Inflammation of bronchial tubes in lungs causing cough and mucus production.
Bronchitis.detailed_advice: Rest, stay hydrated, and avoid irritants. Most cases are viral and resolve on their own.
Bronchitis.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if cough lasts over 3 weeks or if you develop shortness of breath.

Skin Rash.description: Area of irritated or inflamed skin from allergies, infections, or irritants.
Skin Rash.detailed_advice: Identify and avoid triggers. Use soothing lotions and avoid scratching.
Skin Rash.when_to_see_doctor: See dermatologist if rash worsens, spreads, or is accompanied by fever.

Vertigo.description: Sensation of spinning or loss of balance from inner ear or neurological issues.
Vertigo.detailed_advice: Avoid sudden movements. Medication and physical therapy can help.
Vertigo.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if vertigo is severe, persistent, or accompanied by hearing loss.

Dizziness.detailed_advice: Sit or lie down, drink water, and rest. Avoid sudden position changes.
Dizziness.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if dizziness is persistent, severe, or accompanied by chest pain or vision changes.

Fatigue.description: Extreme tiredness impacting daily function from illness, sleep deprivation, or stress.
Fatigue.detailed_advice: Rest adequately, manage stress, and maintain healthy diet. Identify underlying causes.
Fatigue.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if fatigue is persistent and affects daily activities.

Weight Gain.description: Excessive weight gain from poor diet, lack of exercise, hormonal changes, or metabolic disorders.
Weight Gain.detailed_advice: Maintain healthy diet and exercise. Regular activity and proper nutrition manage weight.
Weight Gain.when_to_see_doctor: Consult doctor if weight gain is unexplained or rapid.

Weight Loss.description: Unexplained weight loss from medical conditions, nutritional deficiency, or stress.
Weight Loss.detailed_advice: Eat nutritious foods and identify underlying causes.
Weight Loss.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if weight loss is unexplained or unintended.

Migraine with Aura.description: Migraine with visual disturbances or other sensory symptoms before headache starts.
Migraine with Aura.detailed_advice: Recognize aura as warning sign. Rest and take medication early. Identify triggers.
Migraine with Aura.when_to_see_doctor: See neurology specialist for migraine with aura management.

Diabetes Type 2.description: Chronic disease where body doesn't use insulin effectively (insulin resistance).
Diabetes Type 2.detailed_advice: Weight loss, diet changes, and exercise critical. Medications may be needed.
Diabetes Type 2.when_to_see_doctor: See endocrinologist regularly for management and monitoring.

Flu-like Symptoms.description: General illness symptom combination of fever, fatigue, body aches, and respiratory symptoms.
Flu-like Symptoms.detailed_advice: Could be flu, cold, or other viral infection. Rest and supportive care help.
Flu-like Symptoms.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if symptoms are severe or last over a week.

Diabetes.description: Chronic disease with elevated blood glucose levels affecting organs over time.
Diabetes.detailed_advice: Monitor blood sugar regularly as prescribed. Medication, diet, and exercise crucial.
Diabetes.when_to_see_doctor: Consult doctor for excessive thirst, urination, weight loss, or out-of-range readings.

Malaria.description: Life-threatening disease from parasites transmitted by mosquito bites.
Malaria.detailed_advice: Requires immediate medical treatment with prescription antimalarial drugs.
Malaria.when_to_see_doctor: Seek emergency care for high fever and chills after tropical travel.

Conjunctivitis.description: Inflammation of eye membrane from infection or allergy (pink eye).
Conjunctivitis.detailed_advice: Avoid touching eyes and practice good hygiene. Avoid sharing personal items.
Conjunctivitis.when_to_see_doctor: See doctor if eye pain, light sensitivity, blurred vision, or no improvement.

PCOS.description: Hormonal disorder in women with irregular periods and elevated androgen levels.
PCOS.detailed_advice: Lifestyle modification is primary. Medication addresses specific concerns.
PCOS.when_to_see_doctor: Consult doctor about menstrual concerns, infertility, or excess androgen signs.
